explanation: Heat moves three ways; this scene shows conduction quantitatively with convection and radiation as labeled accents. Conduction carries heat through a solid slab from the hot side to the cold side, and the flow rate Q/t equals the conductivity k times the area A times the temperature difference delta T, divided by the thickness L. Raise k (copper conducts far better than wood) or delta T and the heat-flow arrows speed up; make the slab thicker (bigger L) and the rate drops — that's exactly why insulation is thick and made of low-k material.
bullets: Q/t = k·A·ΔT / L: faster flow with higher conductivity, more area, or a bigger temperature gap.
A thicker slab (larger L) slows conduction — the principle behind insulation.
Conduction needs contact; convection carries heat in moving fluid; radiation needs no medium.
